title: Magic ring — the adjustable start for in-the-round work
subtitle: A slip loop that closes completely — no centre hole left over
excerpt: The magic ring (also called adjustable ring or magic loop) creates a small adjustable circle that closes to nothing when the tail is pulled. Unlike a chain ring, it leaves no hole in the centre — essential for amigurumi, flat circles, and any motif where a neat closed centre is wanted.

glossaryTerms.definition: An adjustable starting loop for in-the-round crochet. Wrap the yarn in a circle around two fingers, insert the hook through the loop and work the first-round stitches over both the loop and the tail. Pull the tail to close the ring after the round is complete. No hole remains.

content.text: is the standard way to start any flat circle, amigurumi piece, or granny motif where a visible centre hole is unwanted. The ring is adjustable because the tail end of the yarn is what closes it — after working the first round over the open loop, pulling the tail draws the ring shut with no gap left.
Hold the yarn tail over the left index and middle fingers. Wrap the working yarn (from the ball) around both fingers once to make a circle.
Insert the hook under the loop on the fingers (under both strands of the circle). Catch the working yarn and draw a loop through — 1 loop on hook. Ch 1 to secure.

Carefully slide the ring off the fingers, holding it from below. Work the first round by inserting into the ring (through the open circle) for each stitch — work over both strands of the ring plus the tail.
After completing all stitches of round 1, pull the tail end to draw the ring closed. Then sl st or continue to round 2.

items.symptom: Ring unravels when removing from fingers
items.cause: The securing ch 1 was not worked, or the ring slipped before the first stitch
items.fix: Work the securing ch 1 before removing the ring from the fingers. Hold the tail and the ring base firmly between thumb and middle finger as the first few stitches are made.

items.symptom: Centre does not close fully when the tail is pulled
items.cause: Some stitches were worked into the ring loop but not over the tail
items.fix: All first-round stitches must enclose both the ring loop and the tail. Hold both together as you insert for each stitch.

content.text: The chain ring is an alternative start: ch 4, sl st to first ch to make a small ring. It is simpler to execute but leaves a small central hole. For amigurumi and flat motifs, magic ring is preferable.
